target: new: degree of a value (hardly, scarcely, slightly, moderately)
reason: Says that raised (PATO_0001369) holds only to a low degree, so the vein is almost flush with the surface. The approximate-value qualifiers (approximately, nearly, almost, sub) don't fit, and 'not raised' would overstate it.

'Veinlets indiscernible' means they cannot be clearly seen, the same reading as the earlier rules for obscure and indistinct. Restrict the rule to veins: the French follicle example ('devenant indiscernables à la base') means merging, not visibility.

target: new: compound of values of different attributes (colour white PATO_0000323 + continuum sericeous PATO_0104358 / villous FLOPO:0991051, docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: A compound word that gives the colour of the indumentum and a hair type between sericeous and villous. Each part has a term, so it should be split rather than given a new class.
'Rather' softens 'thin' the same way '±' and '-ish' do. The value is decreased thickness, with 'rather' as the cue.
A part, not a quality. 'Bearing spikelets almost to the base' states that spikelets are present at a place on the panicle branch.
A process, not a quality. The quality in these statements is epigeal or hypogeal germination of the seedling, which needs its own candidate.
'Stem none' and 'costa none' state that the part is absent. 'Variegation none' is the absence of a quality and should be handled as a negation.
Pattern 17 already uses oblate for plane shapes with a length:width ratio below 1, so 'broadly' adds nothing that needs a separate term.
A half-shrub is a suffrutex: woody only at the base, with herbaceous upper shoots. This is the existing FLOPO growth-form class.
A faint tinge of a colour, treated like 'greenish' (colour with the approximately qualifier). No new colour class is needed.
An indefinite count in the word (arms numerous), like 'few-flowered'. The counted part (trichome arm) needs a bearer; failing that, branched (PATO_0000402) on the trichome is the safe reading.

target: new: depth and order of division (sinus depth; see docs/annotation-context-patterns.md, open proposals)
reason: The bearer is the sinus of a lobed blade, which has no PO class, and 'moderately' is a degree of increased depth (PATO_0001596). This is the open 'depth of division' pattern.

target: new: compound of values of different attributes (angular PATO_0001977 + smooth PATO_0000701 on the angles)
reason: The culm is angled and its angles are smooth (not scabrous). That is two qualities, one of them about a region of the bearer, not one term.
Says only that the spacing is not constant, without a value or a second term. It cannot be told apart from leaving the character unstated.
Denies only one kind of ridge, and 'ridge' is a generic part (rejected in the previous review). 'Not ridged' (PATO_0002358) would overstate it, because the seed may have other ridges.
Bearing sori means sori are present (fertile frond), the same form as lenticellate = lenticel present.

label: camphor-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having a sharp, aromatic odour like that of camphor.
reason: A specific odour, worded like its siblings sweet-scented (FLOPO:0991016) and spicy-scented (FLOPO:0991017). If a new class is not wanted, aromatic (PATO_0002191) is the broader fallback.

target: docs/odp/00-part-and-quality.md (bearer gland = portion of secretory tissue PO_0005656 on the organ; quality sparse PATO_0001609)
reason: A part plus a quality: the glands on the stem, petiole or leaflet are sparse. The bearer rule for gland and PATO sparse already cover both halves.
A stage of leaf expansion, probably relative to flowering, with an open fraction. It is not a quality of the leaf and the stage it refers to isn't stated.

label: filiferous
definition: An edge shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's margin separating into or bearing coarse, often curling threads. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0040008 fringed; nonfiliferous is its negation.
reason: Palm and Yucca leaf margins are described as filiferous or nonfiliferous. PATO filamentous (PATO_0001360) is a cell quality and fringed is not the same. Add 'filiferous' and read the word as its negation.
A plain negation of PATO folded, the same form as unlobed = not lobed.

target: new: compound of values of different attributes (loose PATO_0001802 + panicle inflorescence PO_0030123)
reason: A lax ('open') inflorescence that is a panicle: loose (whose RELATED synonym is lax) plus the PO inflorescence type. Both have terms.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum, as 'linear-lanceolate': pilose FLOPO:0991048 - setose PATO_0002289)
reason: A hyphenated pair of indumentum values describing hairs between pilose and setose, handled like 'linear-lanceolate'.
A self-supporting plant or scape stands without leaning on or twining round another object, which is the negation of climbing. 'Erect' would claim more than that.

target: new: before and after a stage (docs/annotation-context-patterns.md, kind A2)
reason: Flowering relative to leaf emergence is a time relation between two stages, which the open 'before/after a stage' pattern is meant to hold. It is not a quality term.
A stem base swollen like a bulb or corm is PATO bulbous (bulb-shaped). 'Not bulbous-cormose' then goes through the negation slot.

target: new: compound of values of different attributes (keel-shaped PATO_0002522 + callose FLOPO:0991215 on the keel)
reason: A keeled sepal or petal whose keel becomes hard and thickened. The two values exist, and 'becoming' is a transition.

target: new: compound of values of different attributes (banded PATO_0001946 + green PATO_0000320 + white PATO_0000323)
reason: A colour pattern (PATO banded, whose synonym is striped) together with its two colours. The terms exist, and a merged class would only repeat them.

target: new: part present on a surface (stoma on the abaxial and, in part, the adaxial epidermis)
reason: Says how stomata are spread over the two surfaces. FLOPO has no hypostomatous or amphistomatous either, so the three should be modelled together as stomata present on a surface rather than as a one-off term.
Denies a generic part ('projection' was rejected in the previous review) on an unclear bearer ('microscale'). Neither absence of a part nor 'smooth' can be stated firmly.
